text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P0 — Dedicated pool 'acme-enterprise-prod' reporting 98% GPU utilization, single tenant 'acme' is consuming most slots. Paging oncall. thread=4387654321
Anna (oncall-sre): ack — I'm on it. pulling metrics now, will check autoscaler logs and active allocations.
Lee (infra): seeing sustained allocation increase from acme over the last 12m, autoscaler did not scale — pool has hard max of 16 gpus configured. looks like we hit hard cap.
Anna (oncall-sre): command I ran:```bash
rwi admin pool show --pool acme-enterprise-prod --format json | jq '.gpu_usage, .max_gpus, .allocations | length'
```
result: usage 98%, max_gpus 16, active_allocations 312.
Tom (SRE Lead): suggestion: enable short-term burst capacity to avoid customer errors while we decide long-term. options: (1) temporary burst extra GPUs from burst pool (2) preempt lower-priority tenants (not great for multitenant) (3) route heavy requests to quantized model variant.
Karen (acct-eng): acme is on enterprise SLA — they can't have failures right now, please prioritize non-preemptive options. I'm on call with their infra lead and will update them after we have a mitigation plan.
Lee (infra): quick check — burst pool has 8 spare GPUs but current policy requires approval. we can do a 30m burst + autoscale cap increase if SRE approves. command:```bash
rwi admin pool set-burst --pool acme-enterprise-prod --add 4 --duration 30m --reason "emergency acme burst"
```
Anna (oncall-sre): I propose: enable +4 GPUs burst immediately, enable routing fallback for non-critical requests to model-quantized-small (saves ~40% memory), and start throttling low-priority batching. that should get us under 80% quickly. who can approve the burst?
Tom (SRE Lead): I approve a single 4-GPU burst for 30m. make sure OpsBot starts evasion rules for other tenants if needed. also add a canary route to ensure no regressions.
Mike (PM): please coordinate an immediate status ping to acme with ETA 30m and mitigation steps. I'll draft the message.
Anna (oncall-sre): applying burst now...```bash
rwi admin pool set-burst --pool acme-enterprise-prod --add 4 --duration 30m --ticket 2026-INC-4921
```
OpsBot: action taken — burst request queued and executed by capacity-manager v2.0. :white_check_mark:
Anna (oncall-sre): enabling fallback routing rule for non-critical inference paths:```yaml
routing:
  - match: request.path contains "/batch"
    action: route_to model:acme/ggml-quantized-small
    priority: low
```
Lee (infra): also lowering batch size for ephemeral queues: `rwi config set --pool acme-enterprise-prod --batch-size 8` — applied.
Anna (oncall-sre): metrics update: GPU usage dropped from 98% -> 72% within 3m after burst + routing. queue wait times reduced. keeping an eye on evictions.
Karen (acct-eng): acme on call says errors dropped and they're seeing degraded latency on large batches (acceptable). putting them on notice for postmortem.
Tom (SRE Lead): next steps: (A) keep burst for full 30m, (B) open follow-up ticket to raise pool soft-limit and review tenant quotas, (C) evaluate adding a per-tenant cap alert to avoid recurrence. I'll create the follow-up tickets.
Mike (PM): I'll prepare a short customer message: "We activated temporary capacity and routing to reduce impact; investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline and RCA." sending it now.
Anna (oncall-sre): passing handoff to Lee at 15:12 UTC — current state: burst +4 active until +30m, GPU usage 70-75%, no evictions, queued low-priority requests throttled. Lee take over for the watch window.
Lee (infra): taking over. I'll extend monitoring, confirm burst expiry logs, and prepare rollback plan. if utilization creeps >85% I'll start preempting best-effort jobs with warning.
OpsBot: automated note: new alert rule created "tenant_acme_gpu_quota_exceeded" to fire at 85% for 5m.
Anna (oncall-sre): thanks — final note for incident timeline: root cause suspected: acme pushed large training-style batched requests due to recent client-side misconfiguration; not autoscaler bug per se, but pool hard cap blocked automatic remedy. will confirm with allocation logs.
Tom (SRE Lead): please include allocation trace `alloc_id` samples and autoscaler triggers in the postmortem.
Lee (infra): copy. collecting logs now: `rwi admin logs --pool acme-enterprise-prod --since 30m | grep alloc`
Karen (acct-eng): customer follow-up scheduled in 2h. I'll coordinate a joint postmortem invite.
Anna (oncall-sre): IncidentBot: marking incident as mitigated — pool usage stable at 68% after graceful demote of heavy batches and burst ended naturally. monitoring for 30m before close. :tada:
IncidentBot: Incident 4387654321 — mitigation complete. Please file a postmortem with root cause analysis and remediation plan.
Mike (PM): thumbs up. I'll own the customer-facing RCA draft.
Tom (SRE Lead): thanks everyone — great quick coordination.
OpsBot: Reminder: create follow-up tasks: [increase soft cap][add per-tenant hard quota check][improve surge runbook].
